question: How many distinct people do the author records named "Mara Ellison", "M. Ellison" and "Ellison, Mara J." stand for?
expected: Two: Mara Ellison (A01, A02, A03, one ORCID) and a different M. Ellison (A04, at Kesting University, another ORCID).
tests: Identity: A01, A02 and A03 share an ORCID; A04, also 'M. Ellison', has another.

question: List every work, of any type, that Mara Ellison (A01) is an author of.
expected: W01, W04, W05, W06, W12 (as A01), W02, W07, W19 (as A02) and W03 (as A03); not W08 or W16, by A04, a different M. Ellison.
tests: Identity: her works are spread over three author records, and A04's works (W08, W16) are not hers.

question: Is the Jonas Brandt who wrote W37 the same person as the Jonas Brandt who wrote W38?
expected: No. A05 (Albury Metropolitan University) and A06 (Université de Lorvain) have different ORCIDs.
tests: Identity: the same name, different ORCIDs.

question: How many research works has the Jonas Brandt of Albury Metropolitan University (A05) authored?
expected: Two: W14 and W37.
tests: Identity: the other Jonas Brandt's works (W28, W34, W38) are not his.

question: Is the M. Ellison who wrote W08 the same person as the Mara Ellison who wrote W01?
expected: No. W08's author is A04, whose ORCID differs from Mara Ellison's (A01, A02, A03).
tests: Identity: a name variant shared with a different person.

question: Which author has the most research works credited to the University of Albury, its units included?
expected: Mara Ellison (A01 = A02 = A03): W01, W03, W06, W12 and W19. Priya Ramanathan (A07) has four.
tests: Identity: Mara Ellison's five works are split over three records; by record, Priya Ramanathan (four) would come first.

question: How many research works has Mara Ellison authored?
expected: Five: W01, W03 (with its preprint W02), W06, W12 and W19. W04 is an editorial, W05 an erratum, and W07 appeared in a delisted (K0) source.
tests: Everything at once: identity, versions (W02 is W03), document types (W04, W05) and the delisted source (W07).

question: What is the ultimate parent of the Tessel Laboratory for Ocean Sensing (I04)?
expected: The Albury University System (I01): I04 is under I03, under I02, under I01.
tests: Hierarchy: three levels up, lab to centre to university to system.

question: How many research works is the University of Albury (I02) credited with, its units included?
expected: Eight: W01, W03, W06, W12, W13, W19, W71 and W72.
tests: Hierarchy: the labs' works count, each work once; also versions, types, the affiliation rule and the affiliated institute.

question: How many research works is the Albury University System (I01) credited with, all its units included?
expected: Twelve: the University of Albury's eight, plus W14, W28, W29 and W37 from Albury Metropolitan University.
tests: Hierarchy: both universities and their labs, a work shared between them (W12) counted once.

question: How many research works is Kesting University (I07) credited with, its units included?
expected: Six: W08, W16, W20, W21, W22 and W24.
tests: Hierarchy with retraction and test records: the institute's W24 counts; W23 (retracted) and W90 to W92 (STG) don't.

question: How many research works did Kesting University (I07, units included) publish in 2024, under full counting and under fractional counting (each work split equally among its authors)?
tests: Counting method: W20 is half Kesting's, W21 two quarters, W22 whole.

question: In 2024, which had more research works, Kesting University (I07) or Rostval Technical University (I09): under full counting, and under fractional counting?
expected: Full: Rostval, 4 to 3. Fractional: Kesting, 2 to 1, since each of Rostval's four works has four authors and only one of them from Rostval.
tests: Counting method: the ranking flips.

question: How many research works did GB institutions publish in 2024, under full counting and under fractional counting (each work split equally among its authors, each author's share going to their institution's country)?
expected: Full: 7 (W06, W12, W13, W28, W29, W71, W72). Fractional: five whole works plus half of W28 and half of W29 = 6.
tests: Counting method at country level.

question: How many research works appeared in Ocean Sensing Letters (S02) in 2024?
expected: Four: W12, W21, W28 and W51.
tests: Document types: the erratum W05 and the front matter W10 are not research output.

question: How many research works appeared in the Journal of Marine Autonomy (S01)?
tests: Document types: an editorial (W04) and paratext (W09) are not research output; also a test record (W91).

question: Which of Mara Ellison's works are not research output because of their document type?
expected: W04, an editorial, and W05, an erratum.
tests: Document types: an editorial and an erratum, under two author records.

question: How many distinct research works has Priya Ramanathan (A07) authored?
expected: Four: W01, W03 (with its preprint W02), W13 and W72.
tests: Versions: W02 is the preprint of W03; also the erratum W05 is not a work of research.

question: How many distinct works cite "Drift-aware mapping with low-cost sonar", in either of its versions?
expected: Seven: W12, W13, W14, W15, W16, W17 and W18.
tests: Versions: citations to the preprint W02 and to W03 are citations of one work; W15 cites both and counts once.

question: Which works in the data are preprints of another work that is also in the data?
expected: W02 (of W03) and W42 (of W31).
tests: Versions: a shared title is the clue, version_of the evidence; W18 is a preprint with no published version.

question: How many research works is Oskel Polytechnic (I14) credited with?
expected: Four: W27, W31 (with its preprint W42), W39 and W50.
tests: Versions: W42 is the preprint of W31.

question: Which has more citations, W30 or W31 (counting both versions of each): in total, and within its publication year and the two years after?
expected: In total W30 (5 to 4). Within three years W31 (4, from 2023 to 2025, one of them citing its preprint W42) against W30's 1 (2019 to 2021).
tests: Citation windows: the older work has had more time; over the same span the newer one leads.

question: How many citations has W30 received in total, and how many within its publication year and the two years after?
expected: Five in total (W60 to W64); one, W60 (2020), within 2019 to 2021.
tests: Citation windows: a citation's year is the citing work's year.

question: How many research works has Lena Vossberg (A09) authored?
expected: Three: W20, W21 and W22. W23 was retracted.
tests: Retractions: W23 is retracted.

question: What is the total of the citation counts of Lena Vossberg's research works?
expected: Six: W20 three, W21 two, W22 one.
tests: Retractions and test records: W23's citation (W39) doesn't count, nor do the STG works citing W22.

question: Does W23 count towards Kesting University's research output?
expected: No: it has been retracted.
tests: Retractions: a retracted work is not research output.

question: Which other institution's works cite Kesting University's research works the most, each citing work counted once per institution, and how many of its works do?
expected: Université de Lorvain (I12), with three works (W33, W34, W35). Rostval has one work (W32) with four authors, Brevin one (W36) citing two Kesting works.
tests: Citations rolled up: Rostval's one citing work has four Rostval authors; counted per author it would win.

question: How many distinct works from Rostval Technical University (I09) cite Kesting University's research works?
expected: One: W32, which has four authors from Rostval.
tests: Citations rolled up: a work counts once, not once per author.

question: Of the works citing "Drift-aware mapping with low-cost sonar" (either version), how many are self-citations at the level of authors, of the University of Albury (units included), and of countries?
expected: Author: 2 (W12 by Mara Ellison, W13 by her co-author Priya Ramanathan). University of Albury: 2 (the same). GB: 4 (also W14 and W15).
tests: Self-citation depends on the level; W12 is Mara Ellison under another record, W13 her co-author; W16 is the other M. Ellison.

question: Of the works citing "Drift-aware mapping with low-cost sonar" (either version), how many are self-citations at the level of the Albury University System?
expected: Three: W12, W13 and W14 (Albury Metropolitan University, in the same system).
tests: Self-citation at a level between institution and country.

question: Which works cite at least one of the works that cite W01?
expected: W50, W51 and W52 (citing W40 or W41, which cite W01). W90 also cites W41, but it is a test record.
tests: Two hops; W51 cites both first-hop works; W90 is a test record.

question: How many distinct works are within two citation hops of W01 (citing it, or citing a work that cites it)?
expected: Five: W40 and W41, then W50, W51 and W52.
tests: Two hops, counted once each.

question: Which of Kesting University's research works has the most citations?
expected: W20, with three (W32, W35, W36). W22 has one real citation; the other three are STG test records.
tests: Local rule: STG records are test data; with them W22 would lead.

question: How many research works was Kesting University (units included) credited with in 2025?
expected: Three: W08, W16 and W24 (a supplement article). W90 to W92 are test records.
tests: Local rules: STG records are test data; SUP is a research article.

question: How many research works is the Kesting Institute of Hydrodynamics (I08) credited with?
expected: Two: W21 and W24 (SUP, a supplement article).
tests: Local code: SUP is a supplement article, research output, not supplementary material.

question: How many research works appeared in the Proceedings of the Hydrodynamics Forum (S06)?
expected: Two: W17 and W24, both supplement articles. W76 is an editorial.
tests: Local code: both SUP works count; the foreword (EDT) doesn't.

question: Which institution is W70 credited to?
expected: The Halloran Institute for Coastal Studies (I06), listed second, after the Tessel Laboratory.
tests: Local rule: only the affiliation listed last counts.

question: Which institutions is W71 credited to, at every level?
expected: The Tessel Laboratory (I04) and the institutions above it: I03, I02 and I01. Not Halloran (I06), listed first.
tests: Local rule on affiliations, then the hierarchy: the Tessel Laboratory is listed last, so Halloran gets nothing.

question: How many of the University of Albury's research works (units included) appeared in a source of the highest tier?
expected: Three, in the Journal of Marine Autonomy (K3): W01, W13 and W71.
tests: Local code: the tiers count upwards, K3 the highest.

question: Which source is in the highest tier?
expected: The Journal of Marine Autonomy (S01), tier K3.
tests: Local code: K3 is the highest tier, not K1.

question: Is Coastal Engineering Review (S03) in a higher tier than Ocean Sensing Letters (S02)?
expected: No: S03 is K1, the lowest tier; S02 is K2.
tests: Local code: K1 is below K2.

question: How many research works appeared in Global Marine Science Reports (S04)?
expected: None: S04 is delisted (K0), so W07 and W75 don't count.
tests: Local code: K0 is a delisted source, whose works are not research output.

question: Is W07 research output?
expected: No: it is an article, but it appeared in Global Marine Science Reports, a delisted (K0) source.
tests: Local code: an article in a delisted source.

question: Which institutions are part of the Albury University System, at any level below it?
expected: I02, I03, I04 and I05. The Halloran Institute (I06) is an affiliated institute, not a unit.
tests: Local type: an affiliated institute (AFF) is not a unit of its parent.

question: How many research works is the Halloran Institute for Coastal Studies (I06) credited with?
expected: Three: W70, W73 and W74.
tests: Local rule on affiliations: W71 lists Halloran first, so it goes to the Tessel Laboratory.

question: What is the ultimate parent of the Halloran Institute for Coastal Studies (I06)?
expected: Itself (I06): as an affiliated institute it is not a unit of the University of Albury.
tests: Local type: an affiliated institute's parent link is an agreement, not membership.

question: Why do Kesting University and Rostval Technical University swap places in 2024 between full and fractional counting?
expected: Rostval is on four 2024 works (W21, W27, W28, W29), but on each it has one author of four: 4 x 1/4 = 1. Kesting is on three, with larger shares: W22 alone, half of W20, two of the four authors of W21: 2.
tests: Counting method: why the ranking flips.
checklist: Says each of Rostval's four 2024 works has four authors with only one from Rostval, so a quarter each
Says Kesting holds larger shares: a single-author review (W22) and half of W20 and W21

question: Why is W70 not one of the University of Albury's research works, though its author lists the Tessel Laboratory?
expected: Tomasz Wierzba lists the Tessel Laboratory first and the Halloran Institute second; the house rule credits the last-listed one, Halloran. Halloran is an affiliated institute (AFF): its parent link is an agreement, so its works are not the University of Albury's.
tests: Local rules: the last-listed affiliation, and affiliated institutes.
checklist: Says only the affiliation listed last counts, so W70 is credited to the Halloran Institute
Says the Halloran Institute is an affiliated institute, not a unit, so its works don't roll up to the University of Albury
